title: The Sapir-Whorf Hypothesis and Linguistic Relativity in Hungarian

sections.title: Philosophical & Societal Framework
sections.content: The Sapir-Whorf hypothesis proposes that the structure of a language influences its speakers' worldview and cognitive processes. The 'strong' version (linguistic determinism) claims language dictates what we can think; the modern 'weak' version claims language gently guides our attentional habits and perceptual salience.

sections.title: Linguistic Analysis
sections.content: In Hungarian, verbal prefixes (*meg-, el-, ki-, be-, át-, fel-, le-*) do not merely mark completion (telicity); they mark the direction, the boundary and the result of an action (*akcióminőség* / Aktionsart): *kiolvas* (reads to the end), *átolvas* (reads through), *félreolvas* (misreads). Whether this makes Hungarian speakers attend to boundaries and results more than others is debated.
